content.text:
My analysis is complete. The findings:

**The commitment exists** — § 5(a) (p0045) imposes a monthly minimum on Client ("not less than $____ per month" for Hosting and for Support Services), payable regardless of actual usage. So this is a genuine minimum purchase commitment on us, not a Vendor-side commitment (the "not less than ____ months" of programmer availability in p0043 runs in our favour and is not flagged).

**But the exit exists too**, which is what the fallback requires:
- **Limited to the current 12-month term** — § 13 (p0078) runs one year, then auto-renews in successive one-year periods, with either party able to give 30 days' notice of non-renewal. The minimum never extends beyond the term we are currently in.
- **Unilateral exit on roughly a month's notice** — § 14 (p0079) lets Client elect to terminate at will, with services (and therefore the minimum) running only to the last day of the month following notice. That is a termination right stronger than a mere volume reduction.
- **No shortfall penalty** — there is no make-whole, no accelerated payment of unused minimums, and no take-or-pay recapture anywhere. Termination simply stops the monthly minimum going forward, which is functionally a true-up rather than a penalty.

This lands on the fallback position, so under the playbook's classification semantics it is not redlined.

input.quote: Client will pay TrueLink's fees for requested Hosting Services and Support Services pursuant to the schedule of charges set forth on Exhibits "A" and "B" attached hereto, (but not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services).
input.rationale:
Section 5(a) does impose a minimum monthly commitment on us (a floor for Hosting Services and for Support Services payable irrespective of actual usage), so this is not the preferred position of usage-only/ordered-services-only fees. However, it sits squarely at the playbook fallback and is therefore not redlined: (i) the commitment is confined to the current 12-month term, because Section 13 runs for one year and renews only in successive one-year periods with a 30-day non-renewal right exercisable by either party; (ii) Section 14 gives us a unilateral at-will termination right, with services and the corresponding minimum continuing only until the last day of the month following the month of our notice — an exit that is stronger than a mere volume reduction on 30 days' notice; and (iii) there is no shortfall penalty, make-whole, or acceleration of unused minimums anywhere in the agreement, so terminating simply stops the minimum prospectively, which operates as a true-up rather than a penalty. This is well clear of the walk-away case of a multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right. Two drafting points noted but not flagged as deviations under this rule: the minimum dollar amounts remain blank ($____) and should be completed with figures reflecting realistic baseline usage before signature; and Section 6 (p0047) carves the minimum monthly fees out of both our right to supporting documentation and our right to contest charges, which is a billing-transparency point better addressed under the audit/disputes rule than here. The "not less than ____ months" of programmer availability in Section 4 is a commitment TrueLink makes to us and runs in our favour, so it is not flagged.</parationale>
